bio: Essays about attention, memory, and the machines we keep. Long-form, once a week, no newsletter pop-up. Formerly a librarian.
style: long paragraphs, semicolons, one concrete image per section, quietly funny, never uses the word content

bio: I write documentation for distributed systems and complain about it in public. Postmortems, diagrams, and the occasional benchmark.
style: numbered steps, quotes error text verbatim, dry asides in parentheses, allergic to adjectives

bio: Cooking from one small kitchen in Leipzig. Recipes tested three times, failures included. Bread, brine, and things that take all day.
style: warm, second person, weights in grams, admits when a batch fails, ends on a question

bio: Walking the long-distance paths of the Western Ghats and writing them down before I forget. Maps, mud, and bus timetables.
style: present tense field notes, distances and altitudes, short sentences, weather first

bio: Digital archivist. Formats rot, checksums lie, and everyone thinks their backup works. Notes from twelve years of migrations.
style: precise, cites standards by number, gentle doom, loves a table

bio: Building a small furniture shop and a smaller software one. Joinery, invoices, and what a workshop teaches you about shipping.
style: practical, measurements in mm, analogies between wood and code, ends with what he would do differently
